Ananyiv Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Odessa Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery, presumed established in the mid-19th century and visible on an 1889 city plan, was demolished between the 1960s and 1980s under Soviet rule, when a regional road management office was built on its grounds; some gravestones were relocated to Ananyiv's still-existing newer cemetery. The Jewish community here endured one of the earliest and most severe pogroms in this region, in April 1881, along with further violence in 1905 and 1919 — the latter partly repelled by a 300-member Jewish self-defense unit, 220 of whom died fighting a Ukrainian nationalist militia. Roughly 3,700 Jews were murdered here during the 1941–1944 Nazi occupation, after a population that had once peaked near 4,800.
